newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INTERVIEW - ANZ Funds sees more growth in N.Zealand.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - ANZ Funds sees more growth in N.Zealand.

text.p: ANZ Funds Management said on Thursday it was New Zealand's fastest growing retail investment manager in 1996 and such growth was only the beginning.
"The exciting thing for us is we think we've only just scratched the surface on our network," General Manager Anthony Quirk told Reuters in an interview.
"I say we can improve on what we've done to date."

Quirk said ANZ was well placed to reach its goal of raising funds under management to NZ$1.5 billion in the year to September, from NZ$1.1 billion at the end of September 1996 and $860 million at the start of 1996.
"We're ahead of budget on that, so we're very pleased," he said, adding that wholesale business had been a key driver.
Quirk said ANZ Funds Management's recent achievement of ISO 9001 quality assurance certification would help it ensure standards did not slip as business boomed.

"It seems to be a trend in New Zealand that fast-growing fund managers find it hard to cope with that growth. We've put the things in place to make sure that doesn't happen and ISO 9001 is part of that, to make sure we have the systems and the people to cope with the growth.
"That's probably our biggest challenge -- to maintain the growth but also to make sure the wheels don't fall off."
Quirk said out of New Zealand's top 10 fund managers, ANZ had enjoyed the largest rise in market share from a year ago. It had moved to sixth place from ninth.
"The top managers in terms of market share have been stagnant and we've been increasing our share, which is good."

In the 1996 IPAC Securities/Money Management Awards ANZ won the inaugural title of "Most Improved Fund Manager". It was third out of 35 managers in the "Fund Manager of the Year" stakes, behind Tower Trust Services and Bankers Trust Funds Management.

Quirk said aiming for the top slot in terms of investment performance would involve courting too much risk. Instead, ANZ aimed for consistent performance over time, and sought to be in the top quarter of fund managers.
ANZ focused on more than simply returns.
"It depends on whether you think the customer service side is important, or whether you think the investment performance is the key to doing well. We think it's both.

"We've tried to differentiate ourselves on our quality, and we believe ISO 9001 is part of that," Quirk said, adding ANZ was the first investment manager in New Zealand, and one of the few in the world, to achieve the international standard.
"We are different, we are distinct and we are a leader. I'd be quite happy for the other managers not to follow."
Quirk said ANZ Funds Management concentrated on picking cheap companies and assets to invest in, rather than shifting funds from sector to sector in a chase for better returns.
"We just set a base portfolio and stick to it, then try and pick cheap companies within that," he said.

"It's obviously a complete contrast to the Southpac (Investment Management) style which they've just announced. They've got the completely opposite view, which is that you index within each one, and then you move around."

In November, ANZ Funds Management added a property trust to its range of unit trusts. The trust invests in shares of property companies rather than owning property itself, which Quirk said provided better liquidity and more diversification.
